chantedPrayers.text: Liberating Prayer O Blessed One, Shakyamuni Buddha, precious Treasury of Compassion, Bestower of Supreme Inner Peace. You who love all beings without exception are the source of happiness and goodness, and you guide us to the liberating path. Your body is a wish-fulfilling jewel, your speech is supreme, purifying nectar, and your mind is refuge for all living beings. With folded palms I turn to you, Supreme unchanging Friend. I request from the depths of my heart, please give me the light of your wisdom to dispel the darkness of my mind and to heal my mental continuum. Please nourish me with your goodness, that I in turn may nourish all beings with an unceasing banquet of delight. Through your compassionate intention, your blessings and virtuous deeds, and my strong wish to rely upon you, may all suffering quickly cease and all happiness and joy be fulfilled, and may holy Dharma flourish forevermore.

guidedMeditation.speaker: Kadam Kyle
guidedMeditation.text:
We can remember that to become enlightened, we need bodhichitta. To develop bodhichitta, we need great compassion, the wish for others to attain permanent liberation from samsara. We cannot wish this for others if we do not have this wish for ourself.

Therefore, we need to increase our renunciation so that we can develop great compassion and bodhichitta, and then attain enlightenment. To increase our renunciation, we need to think about the sufferings of samsara, the fact that we have no satisfaction. We are born alone and die alone.

We have to take rebirth after rebirth in boundless samsara. We have no companionship. Especially, we can meditate on the suffering of uncertainty.

Just go through your life and reflect how everything is uncertain. Certainty is just a complete illusion, because everything is impermanent. Everything is constantly changing.

If we get distracted, just don't give in to this mental resistance. Just really face the truth of uncertainty. Really face the pain and suffering that it brings us and others.

Really try to connect to the fact that samsara is always unstable and uncertain, and how difficult and anxiety-producing this can be. We cannot fix this quality of samsara. It is its nature to be unstable.

Really let that sink in to your heart. If a powerful wish arises to abandon samsara completely, just hold this single-pointedly, this joyful renunciation. Finally, we can think samsara is the nature of suffering.

It is unbearable for me to remain. Therefore, it is unbearable for all living beings to remain in samsara. I must act to free myself and all living beings.

Just make this clear, powerful determination. Then, in our own time, we can gradually arise from our practice.

shantidevReading.text: Chapter 1: An Explanation of the Benefits of Bodhichitta (15) In brief, you should know That bodhichitta has two types: The mind that observes enlightenment and aspires, And the mind that observes enlightenment and engages. (16) Just as the distinction between wishing to go And actually going is understood, So, respectively, the wise should understand The difference between these two bodhichittas. (17) From the mind that aspires to enlightenment, Great effects arise while in samsara; But an uninterrupted flow of good fortune does not ensue As it does from the engaging mind. (18) For whoever takes up the engaging mind of bodhichitta With the intention never to turn back From completely liberating The infinite living beings throughout all realms, (19) From that time forth, for him there will arise – Even if he is asleep or apparently unconcerned – Vast and powerful merit, equal to space, That flows without interruption. (20) For the sake of those with lesser inclinations, These benefits were explained with logical reasons By the Tathagata himself In Sutra Requested by Subahu. (21) If even the thought to relieve The headaches of others Is a beneficial intention That results in infinite merit, (22) What can be said of the wish To dispel the immeasurable misery Of each and every living being And lead them all to countless good qualities? (23) Does our father or mother Have such a beneficial intention as this? Do the gods or the sages? Does even Brahma himself? (24) If, before generating bodhichitta, these living beings Do not even dream of such a mind For their own sakes, How will they develop it for the sake of others? (25) This mind to benefit living beings, Which does not arise in others even for their own sakes, Is an extraordinary jewel of a mind, Whose birth is an unprecedented wonder.

chantedPrayers.text: Liberating Prayer O Blessed One, Shakyamuni Buddha, precious Treasury of Compassion, Bestower of Supreme Inner Peace. You who love all beings without exception are the source of happiness and goodness, and you guide us to the liberating path. Your body is a wish-fulfilling jewel, your speech is supreme, purifying nectar, and your mind is refuge for all living beings. With folded palms I turn to you, Supreme unchanging Friend. I request from the depths of my heart, please give me the light of your wisdom to dispel the darkness of my mind and to heal my mental continuum. Please nourish me with your goodness, that I in turn may nourish all beings with an unceasing banquet of delight. Through your compassionate intention, your blessings and virtuous deeds, and my strong wish to rely upon you, may all suffering quickly cease and all happiness and joy be fulfilled, and may holy Dharma flourish forevermore.

I need to protect the people of Brooklyn, and the world, and the people in hell, and the people who are hungry ghosts, and the animals, and the gods, and the demigods. I need to protect all of them. I'm going to come here to get charged up, and inspired, and get some Dharma teachings, but then I need a mind of outreach and an elevation for my spiritual life.

That's what I need. I need to find a fire in me. It's not enough to just have a comfy club.

Because there are effects of that mind. And the effects are basically that people are just suffering horribly everywhere. So I'm not saying this with respect to this center in particular, or our group in particular, or anything like that.

I'm just saying it in general. It can happen to a Dharma center, that it's so comfortable and nice, that it's just like a little spa that we go to, for a little relief, to make some sorrow more bearable. It's actually a lot more than that, what we're working on here.

Let's see if we can connect to this mind of superior intention. I do think the more we contemplate karma, the more it will feed the superior intention. Let's have time for discussion now.

practiceDiscussion.speaker: Kadam Kyle
practiceDiscussion.text: What would we like to do in the break? What would we like to emphasize?

practiceDiscussion.speaker: Fran
practiceDiscussion.text: One thing I was thinking about is looking at my choices of my non-Dharma activities and what my purpose of them is, even if it's something neutral, and what else I could be doing with that time rather than just sort of hanging out.

practiceDiscussion.speaker: Kadam Kyle
practiceDiscussion.text:
Yeah. Yeah, it's a nice thing to experiment with and explore just in an incredibly non-judgmental way.

Yeah, if we have a tendency towards a potentially hard-on-ourself mind, that kind of thing can go awry really quickly. So we have to kind of know ourself when we're doing a practice like that and tread lightly if we're someone who goes to those places.

Some people don't, in which case it's great. You just let it rip. But for other people, they do.

And then it could be not that effective.

practiceDiscussion.speaker: Adriana
practiceDiscussion.text:
I don't remember how long ago it was, but you gave us an example of thinking about if our life were on a split screen and it was split between hell realm and us. Actually, it's like a big control center, and you can see all the beings from different realms are watching you. And they're like, oh, is that helping us?

Oh, no, Adriana just is drinking more coffee. Yeah. It's not what we want.

Yeah. That could be fun. Yeah.

practiceDiscussion.speaker: Kadam Kyle
practiceDiscussion.text:
It's a really nice kind of practice, especially just trying to be attuned to everyone and more and more people. And it's a little bit like, yeah, you're one little screen, and there's like 99 billion other little screens, and each one is one person. But they're all like suffering in their own ways, and they can see you, what you're up to.

And it's interesting to think, what would they say when I do this? What would they say when I do that? What would they think about when I do this?

What would they think about when I do that? Just attuning our mind to all those people is really healthy and useful. It gets us out of a self-centered mind, an overly self-focused mind.

Okay, and then maybe we can just try to cultivate some superior intention. That's sort of the main point of this section, so let's all work on that. In the break I got a call from one of my sangha friends and her kid who's 13, and they called me like three times in a row.

I was like, oh gosh, third time. It's not a good sign because I know them from the festivals and stuff. And the 13-year-old said she got a call from a friend, but then they were all at a Super Bowl party, and the friend didn't realize that she was still on the phone.

And then the guy and all these other girls that were there just started to say horrible things about her while the phone was still on. And she was so sad. It was just heartbreaking because these were her friends.

And just a great example for me, like, wow, how quick. What can I do? Nothing.

I just said some nice words, you know, and make some prayers. But it's like that's one tiny little sliver of suffering in the world, and that's incredibly painful, just that one tiny sliver. And it's like, okay, what can I do right now?

Well, not much. I can pray, mostly. I need to become a Buddha.

So it was like a great teaching about superior intention, like how quickly it came, you know, within a second of the class. Yeah. So let's work on that mind.

session2.dedication: Through the virtues we've collected through practicing, meditating, discussing. May we become someone who can really protect and liberate all living beings.
